articles.title: A feasibility study to empower patients with individualised physical rehabilitation through wearable technology: The potential of the 'RehabBuddy' system.
articles.authors: Uhl TL, Riemann E, Abu-Raddaha A, Bellaire S, McCallum L, Rawashdeh S
articles.outcomes: Recruitment rate, System Usability Scale scores, technical problems, data completeness, movement errors across three feedback conditions (therapist feedback, no feedback, RehabBuddy feedback)
articles.take_home: The RehabBuddy wearable system was successfully used in a clinic setting and produced usable movement-error measurements for most exercises, but technical problems mean it is not yet ready for patients to use independently at home. Further technical improvements and home-based testing are needed before testing whether it actually improves rehabilitation outcomes.

articles.title: Definitions and reporting of 'failure' after rotator cuff repair: A systematic review of level I and level II evidence and proposal for standardisation.
articles.authors: Cecere M, Chan A, Sritharan P, Hali K, Sheth U
articles.study_type: Systematic review of randomised controlled trials and cohort studies
articles.outcomes: Definitions and reporting methods for failure after rotator cuff repair; failure rates ranged from 0% to over 50% depending on how failure was defined
articles.take_home: Different studies define and measure failure after rotator cuff repair in very different ways, making it hard to compare results. Researchers propose a new standard that combines imaging findings, patient experience and clinical measurements to give a clearer picture of whether repair has worked.
